clue.text: Arranged four by four transport with fussy decoration

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the first four's letters are reshuffled
to transport is to carry away or shift, so the second four's letters are moved about too

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a pair of four-by-four off-road vehicles, oddly with fussy trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four by four transport' reads as a 4x4 vehicle, but each four has its own anagram signal, and 'by' just sets the two results side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou is elaborate, showy ornamentation, especially frills on clothing.

clue.text: Takeaway dish's middle doubled and moved to end to make it sparkle

indicators.text: middle doubled and moved to end
indicators.note: the central letter of the dish is doubled and that pair shifted to the back of the word

parts.note: a pizza is a typical takeaway dish

explanation.surface: A recipe trick: rearrange a takeaway pizza to make it sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of PIZZA is Z; doubling it and moving that ZZ to the end leaves PIZA followed by ZZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizazz is vitality and flair, the quality that makes something sparkle.

clue.text: Whiff toe, turning a sickly colour?

indicators.note: turning means changing round, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whiff from someone's foot makes their toe turn a sickly colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a pale, greyish or yellowish shade, the sort of pallor one calls sickly.

clue.text: Sounds like noise of sneezing head off — absorbing stuff

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: the noise of a sneeze is ATISHOO; with its head, the first letter, off it is TISHOO

explanation.surface: A sneeze sound with its first letter gone resembles absorbent material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the first letter of ATISHOO, the British spelling of a sneeze's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is soft, absorbent material used for wiping and blowing noses.

clue.text: Hand over the city's boxing quarter

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the city wraps round the quarter

parts.note: Turin is the northern Italian city
N, north, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to surrender the city's boxing district.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in something is to hand it over to the authorities.

clue.text: Several times gained by the heartless, grasping filthy rich

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the trimmed word wraps round the other piece
heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed, keeping its first and last
filthy here signals the letters of rich are made a mess of

explanation.surface: The heartless filthy rich grasp at whatever they can gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrice means three times, which counts as several repetitions.

clue.text: Relating to food that's a bit distasteful

definitions.meaning: read as '...', concerning a kind of food
slightly off, as food can be

explanation.surface: Describing food that is slightly unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'of fish' it relates to a food; read as off plus -ish it means slightly bad.

clue.text: "Celebrated 19th century poet" covers MacGonagall finally? Far from it!

indicators.note: covers means one piece goes round another

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the Victorian novelist and poet

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Was McGonagall a celebrated nineteenth-century poet? Far from it!
explanation.walkthrough: William McGonagall is famous as the worst poet in the language, which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly, as an exclamation, means scarcely or not at all, much like far from it.

clue.text: Boxwallah gettin' something off his chest, it's said, to the Creator?

indicators.note: it's said marks the word as spoken rather than written

parts.note: coughin', clearing the chest by coughing
God is the Maker

explanation.surface: A man confesses his troubles to God, as if coughing to the Creator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxwallah' is a playful coinage: a man who deals in boxes, here coffins.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin maker makes boxes for the dead, so is jokingly a box-wallah, a box trader.

clue.text: The woman's usual disguise includes beard, but not one drop of perspiration

indicators.note: includes means the rearranged letters wrap round another piece
a disguise alters appearance, so the letters of usual are rearranged
but not tells us to take one word away from another

parts.note: a bead of sweat

explanation.surface: A woman uses her usual disguise, a false beard, but stays dry.
explanation.walkthrough: BEARD without BEAD leaves R, which goes into USULA, an anagram of USUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula is a woman's first name, so a fair example of a woman.

clue.text: Town of map makers and crossword setters taking Sun test

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
setters speak of themselves as we
S is short for Sunday or sun
a try is an attempt or test

explanation.surface: Map makers and puzzle setters in some town sit a test on the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Oswestry is a market town in Shropshire, near the Welsh border.

clue.text: "Arthur's Cigars" rendered with two lines added

indicators.note: rendered here means turned into something else, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: L stands for line, twice

explanation.surface: Arthur's cigars are drawn with two extra lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Scargill was leader of the British miners' union during the 1984-85 strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Scargill is the British trade unionist, so the surname belongs to an Arthur.

clue.text: Some killer — if fez's turned back, he would call the shots

indicators.note: turned back means the letters read from right to left
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A killer wearing a fez gives orders as if in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'killer if fez' backwards: ZEF FI RELLIK holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franco Zeffirelli was an Italian film director, the one who calls 'Action!' and directs the shots.

clue.text: Useless types writing about foreign cars sought by cinema managers?

parts.note: bums are idle, worthless people
a book on a topic is writing about it
SEAT is a Spanish car maker

explanation.surface: Idlers writing about imported cars attract the interest of cinema managers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bums on seats is the idiom for paying audiences, which cinema managers want.

clue.text: Profile party opinion

parts.note: a side or party to a dispute
a view is an opinion

explanation.surface: The profile of a party's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A side view of a face is its profile, seen from one side.

clue.text: A trigger released whiskery old jazz number

indicators.note: released means set free, so the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pulling a trigger sets off an old jazz tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Rag is a 1917 jazz standard, so whiskery with age.

clue.text: For British abroad, maybe sex is wrong without a bit of butter

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece goes round another
wrong means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a pat of butter is a small portion

explanation.surface: Maybe sex is wrong without a little butter, says the moralist abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British abroad, maybe' is a definition by example: the answer covers anyone living overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Expatriates are people living abroad, such as British living overseas.

clue.text: Like the drunk's speech distributed around farms?

explanation.surface: Slurred drunken speech is likened to muck spread on farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as slur plus -y it describes drunken speech; slurry is also liquid manure spread on fields.

clue.text: In 1920s/30s they easily accommodated male members in neat car loads

definitions.text: In 1920s/30s they easily accommodated male members

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, as an ox
a Ford is a car
bags of something is loads of it

explanation.surface: Men of the interwar years packed their members comfortably into a neat car.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford bags were very wide trousers fashionable in the 1920s and 30s, roomy around the legs.

clue.text: Tile — and what it's use in crossword clues is!

definitions.meaning: tile is old slang for a hat

definitions.text: what it's use in crossword clues is

explanation.surface: Using tile for a hat in crossword clues is a hackneyed device.
explanation.definitionFit: Tile is an outdated term for a hat; and clichéd devices are called stale or hackneyed.

clue.text: Row sailor back to arrive at underside of arch

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a tiff is a row or quarrel
OS, ordinary seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor rows back to reach the underside of an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: A soffit is the underside of an architectural element such as an arch.

clue.text: See 11
Brandy brings a due change in diminutive girl

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Evie is a pet form of Eve or Evelyn

indicators.note: change means alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small girl brings a change that is due.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for water of life, is a clear fruit brandy.

clue.text: Become coated with foreign money — wild excitement!

parts.note: to fur is to become coated, as a kettle furs up
the öre is a Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: Getting coated in foreign money causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public excitement or outrage.

clue.text: Kevin's gap year

parts.note: a space is a gap

explanation.surface: Kevin takes a gap year.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin Spacey is the American actor, so the surname belongs to a Kevin.

clue.text: Nameless European city, back yard address of mistress

indicators.note: nameless removes N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Milan is the Italian city

indicators.note: back means read in reverse

explanation.surface: In a European city, the back yard is the address of a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Milady is a polite form of address to a noblewoman or lady of the house.
